text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.

The first available economic indicators for the first two months of 1997 show a remarkable level of economic stability. The Sao Paulo Industry Federation (FIESP) said yesterday that industrial output had grown, with an upward seasonal adjustment of 0.3 percent from January vs December.
-- MANAUS FREE TRADE ZONE TURNS 30 AND SHOWS ITS AGE
The Manaus Free Trade Zone turns 30 years-old facing a wave of criticism that the model upon which it was constructed is outdated. - - -
-- GOV'T TO SPLIT PROCEEDS FROM CVRD SELLOFF

The federal government agreed to put 50 percent of privatization receipts from Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) into a fund to finance infrastructure projects. The remainder will be used to pay-off public sector debt.
-- CONGRESS WANTS LARGE BANKS TO TESTIFY
A congressional committee looking into a multi-million fraud involving municipal and state bonds is calling representatives from large banks and pension funds which purchased the bonds.
Brazil lost 755,000 jobs since the Real stabilization plan was introduced in July 1994.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
